title: Deep learning on 12-lead ECGs separates sudden cardiac death cases from controls
summary: A 12-lead ECG deep learning model was developed on 1,827 pre-arrest ECGs from 1,796 out-of-hospital sudden cardiac death cases in the Portland area plus control ECGs. It reached an AUROC of 0.889 for cases versus controls in the internal held-out set and 0.820 in an external cohort of 714 cases from Ventura County, versus 0.712 and 0.743 for a conventional six-variable ECG model. The design is case-control with retrospectively collected ECGs; the authors say further investigation is needed before it contributes to risk stratification.

evidence.unknown: Case-control design with retrospectively collected ECGs; prospective use for risk stratification and clinical benefit not shown; full text not reviewed.
